briefing.text: Recurrent TERT promoter mutations (C228T at chr5:1,295,228 and C250T at chr5:1,295,250, hg19) lie upstream of the coding sequence in a GC-rich region that whole-exome capture usually does not cover. Before testing anything, check whether this study records TERT promoter status at all: look for Hugo_Symbol == TERT rows in data_mutations.txt, read each row's Variant_Classification (5'Flank/5'UTR versus coding) and Start_Position, and search the clinical tables for any TERT-related column. A coding TERT variant such as a missense mutation is not a promoter mutation and should not be used in its place.
briefing.reason: Whether the hypothesis variable exists is the central question here. Teams could easily treat any TERT row in the MAF as a promoter mutation, or miss that the assay may never have targeted the promoter.

briefing.text: TERT copy number, TERT expression itself, IDH1-wildtype status or ATRX-wildtype status are not measures of TERT promoter mutation. Expression is the outcome, so using it as a proxy is circular, and the IDH/ATRX links are only correlational. If no direct promoter-status variable exists, any proxy changes the hypothesis being tested and can be reported only as context, not as evidence.
briefing.reason: If the direct variable is missing, building a proxy is the most likely way to reach an unjustified conclusion.

briefing.text: In cBioPortal data, a sample with no mutation row for a gene is not necessarily wildtype; it may not have been profiled. data_gene_panel_matrix.txt contains samples with mutations=NA. Restrict any mutant-vs-wildtype comparison to profiled samples, and confirm that the genomic region of interest was covered by the assay, since absence in an untargeted region carries no information.
briefing.reason: This decides how the comparison groups are defined and whether 'no call' means anything.

briefing.text: TERT mRNA is low in abundance and often zero in RNA-seq, with a bimodal distribution across tumours. Check the fraction of zeros and the skew of the TERT row in data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt. For group comparisons, prefer log2(RSEM+1) with a rank-based test (Mann-Whitney) plus a comparison of the fraction of tumours expressing TERT, rather than t-tests on raw values or on reference-scaled z-scores.
briefing.reason: This is the correct handling of the expression outcome if a valid mutation grouping exists.

briefing.text: TERT can be activated without a promoter mutation, through amplification, rearrangement or promoter hypermethylation, and TERT-promoter-wildtype GBMs are often IDH/ATRX-mutant tumours that differ systematically from the rest. If a genuine promoter-status variable exists, tabulate TERT CNA (data_cna.txt), IDH1 mutation and G-CIMP status by group, and report both crude comparisons and comparisons adjusted or stratified for these (for example, IDH-wildtype only, or excluding TERT-amplified samples).
briefing.reason: These are confounders that could distort a mutant-vs-wildtype expression comparison.

briefing.text: The hypothesis claims there is no correlation. A non-significant test from tiny groups, or from a proxy variable, is absence of evidence, not support for that claim. Report group sizes and an effect size with a confidence interval, and judge whether the test had the power to support or reject the claim.
briefing.reason: This guards against reading an underpowered null result as support for a 'no correlation' hypothesis.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assume that a WXS mutation table with no promoter calls means promoter status was not measured, not that every profiled tumour is promoter-wildtype. They did not show directly that the capture design or the variant filter excludes the TERT upstream region, for example from the coverage or flank-call density near other genes' first exons.

Both teams take 'TERT promoter mutation' strictly as a variant at the upstream hotspot positions. Neither asked whether the task author meant any TERT mutation, or whether the assignment comes from some other field such as a curated subtype or annotation.
Both treat 'Not verifiable' as the right label when the exposure is absent. Neither considered whether the absence of any promoter-mutant group could instead be read as evidence on the claim.
unused_evidence: Clinical sample columns IDH1_MUTATION, G_CIMP_METHYLATION, METHYLATION_STATUS and EXPRESSION_SUBTYPE. In glioma these are strongly linked to TERT promoter status, but they are proxies. Neither team stated explicitly whether any of them encodes promoter status.
TERT copy number (data_cna.txt, data_linear_cna.txt, the seg file). These offer an alternative mechanism for high TERT expression. They are irrelevant to the label unless a promoter variable exists.
The overlap between the one TERT-mutated sample, the mutation-profiled set (gene panel matrix 'mutations' column) and the roughly 150 RNA-seq samples. Neither team reported it.
The upstream_gene_variant and 5_prime_UTR_variant rows in the MAF. They show that some non-coding flank calls were retained, which bears on whether the promoter could have been called at all.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: promoter status might come from data outside these files. The team only reported this and did not resolve it, though it is moot under the given-data rule.

Team B: a promoter status might be hidden in an unscanned field. B scanned the MAF and clinical headers but not the categorical values (e.g. subtype labels) or the RPPA/CNA row names. This was partly resolved.
Neither team showed that the WXS capture would have detected the hotspots if they were present, so 'not measured' versus 'measured and absent' is still asserted, not shown.
second_readings: 'TERT promoter mutations' could be read loosely as 'TERT mutations'. Under that reading the single coding missense sample could be compared with the rest on TERT mRNA. Its n=1 would make any test uninformative, which still points to Not verifiable, but no team said so.
'Elevated mRNA expression' could mean raw RSEM, z-scores against all samples, or z-scores against diploid samples. This matters only if an exposure variable exists.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed 'Not verifiable' fairly well. The MAF is GRCh37, the hotspot window was searched, and the only TERT call is in the gene body, so I found no clear sign of a promoter variable. Both teams scanned headers, not values, and neither showed that the capture could not detect the promoter, so the questions target those two gaps.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: List the distinct values of every categorical column in data_clinical_sample.txt and data_clinical_patient.txt, not only the headers, and the row names of data_rppa.txt. Does any value encode TERT promoter or telomere-maintenance status? Does the result change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Count upstream_gene_variant and 5_prime_UTR_variant calls in data_mutations.txt and how far they lie from transcription start sites. Is there evidence that the WXS calls could include a site about 100-150 bp upstream of a TSS? Does that change whether you read 'no promoter calls' as 'not measured' or as 'measured and wildtype'?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Is the single TERT-mutated sample both mutation-profiled and present in data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt? If the hypothesis is read loosely as 'TERT mutations', could any comparison be made, and would it change your label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You checked clinical headers, not values. Tabulate the values of EXPRESSION_SUBTYPE, METHYLATION_STATUS, G_CIMP_METHYLATION and IDH1_MUTATION, and search all clinical lines, including the # description lines, for TERT, telomer or promoter. Does any field carry promoter status? Does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Count upstream and 5'UTR variant calls in data_mutations.txt and how far they lie from TSSs. Does the MAF show the capture could have detected a TERT upstream hotspot? Does that change whether the absence is 'unmeasured' or 'measured wildtype', and does that affect your label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Report the overlap between mutation-profiled samples (gene panel matrix), RNA-seq samples and the one TERT-mutated sample. Under a loose 'any TERT mutation' reading, is a comparison possible at all, and does it change your label?

Do standard whole-exome capture kits from about 2008-2012, and the somatic variant pipelines used with them, typically cover and call the TERT core promoter hotspots (about 124 and 146 bp upstream of the ATG)?
questions.why: This settles whether the absence of promoter calls in WXS data means 'not measured' or 'measured and wildtype', which separates Not verifiable from an evidence-based label.

questions.question: In public cancer-genomics portals, how is TERT promoter mutation status usually distributed for studies that have it: as a MAF row with a 5'Flank/upstream class, as a clinical sample attribute, or as a separate table?
questions.why: This tells the teams where a promoter variable would sit if one existed, so they can confirm none is present.

findings.question: In public cancer-genomics portals, how is TERT promoter mutation status usually distributed for studies that have it: as a MAF row with a 5'Flank/upstream class, as a clinical sample attribute, or as a separate table?
findings.answer: In cBioPortal there are two conventions, and a separate table is not one of them. (1) MAF rows: TERT promoter variants are kept as data_mutations rows on gene TERT (Entrez 7015) with Variant_Classification 5'Flank. The cBioPortal loader's mutation filter drops 5'Flank mutations except for TERT, which is whitelisted, and sets the protein change to 'Promoter'. This is typical for targeted-panel studies whose assay covers the promoter. (2) Clinical sample attribute: TCGA whole-exome MAFs generally lack TERT promoter calls, because those came from separate targeted assays. cBioPortal datahub issue #154 states that TCGA studies including LGG/GBM did not have this data loaded. Where curators later added it (e.g. thca_tcga_pub, PR #1753, 2023), they used a 'TERT' clinical variable taken from the paper's supplementary table. For a TCGA-style GBM study, the teams should look for TERT rows with 5'Flank or 'Promoter' in data_mutations.txt and for any TERT* column in the clinical files. If neither exists, the dataset has no promoter variable.
findings.text: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In public cancer-genomics portals, how is TERT promoter mutation status usually distributed for studies that have it: as a MAF row with a 5'Flank/upstream class, as a clinical sample attribute, or as a separate table? ANSWER: In cBioPortal there are two conventions, and a separate table is not one of them. (1) MAF rows: TERT promoter variants are kept as data_mutations rows on gene TERT (Entrez 7015) with Variant_Classification 5'Flank. The cBioPortal loader's mutation filter drops 5'Flank mutations except for TERT, which is whitelisted, and sets the protein change to 'Promoter'. This is typical for targeted-panel studies whose assay covers the promoter. (2) Clinical sample attribute: TCGA whole-exome MAFs generally lack TERT promoter calls, because those came from separate targeted assays. cBioPortal datahub issue #154 states that TCGA studies including LGG/GBM did not have this data loaded. Where curators later added it (e.g. thca_tcga_pub, PR #1753, 2023), they used a 'TERT' clinical variable taken from the paper's supplementary table. For a TCGA-style GBM study, the teams should look for TERT rows with 5'Flank or 'Promoter' in data_mutations.txt and for any TERT* column in the clinical files. If neither exists, the dataset has no promoter variable. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: https://github.com/cBioPortal/cbioportal/issues/895, https://github.com/cBioPortal/datahub/issues/154, https://github.com/cBioPortal/datahub/pull/1753.
